content.comment_body: Hello, Has anyone successfully established communication between [product_name] and [product_name] using [version_no] (V12/7.2/7.0)? If so, could you share the system architecture and details on how it was achieved? I'm considering using an OPC server and have found one—can someone confirm if it will work with [company_name] [product_name] SCADA? [url] Alternatively, is there another available method to achieve this? The goal is to monitor and control 28 units of [product_name] (with modules) in a SCADA environment.

Hi, One option is using the S7-200 PC-Access, which is an OPC server for S7-200, though it has certain restrictions, such as only supporting WinXP Sp2. It also requires TSAP 21.00 or a higher configuration in [product_name]. Another method would be to utilize Net OPC-Server. Hope this information is helpful.
If I use the S7-200 OPC, will I be able to communicate or integrate it with SCADA? Also, could you clarify the concept of lean PC? How can it be connected to [product_name]?

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are looking for reliable ways to connect [product_name] hardware (with modules) to [product_name] SCADA systems using OPC servers. There's uncertainty about OPC server compatibility and system requirements, with users seeking advice on which solutions fit their needs. Questions also arise regarding integration between specific hardware and software options, revealing a need for clearer documentation and compatibility guidance for connecting [product_name] and [product_name] SCADA.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are hoping for a simple, officially supported integration between [product_name] and [product_name] SCADA via an OPC server, with clear instructions on system architecture and compatibility for particular software versions and operating systems. They expect to reliably monitor and control multiple devices within a SCADA system.
